section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A pre-operational child, when asked to describe what a doll placed across the table 'sees', describes the scene exactly as the child themselves sees it, unable to imagine the doll's different viewpoint. This inability to take another's perspective is called:
explanation: Egocentrism (demonstrated in Piaget's classic 'three mountains' task) is the inability of a pre-operational child to see a situation from another person's perspective — distinct from centration, which is focusing on only one dimension of a problem at a time.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A formal-operational adolescent, when given a science problem, can systematically generate and test multiple 'if-then' possibilities in their head before experimenting, rather than trying things randomly. This systematic, abstract problem-solving ability is called:
explanation: Hypothetico-deductive reasoning is the hallmark of Piaget's formal operational stage — systematically generating and testing hypotheses in the abstract before acting, unlike younger children's trial-and-error approach.
